text:
Hey Amy - I'm so sorry to hear about this. I can imagine how frustrating it is. Five months is too long, much longer than the average time for entry permission. If your partner hasn't emailed PIBA, I think he should try this (include his TZ and your passport details) - for Tel Aviv, he can try Ahmash-TLV@piba.gov.il and Ashrot51@piba.gov.

I also think he should continue to go in person. Even though this can seem futile after the previous attempts, this really can help move the application forward. When he speaks with the clerk, he should inquire about the reason for the long delay and, if necessary, request to be attended to assertively. Once he has more information about the reason for the hold-up, you might be able to come back here and seek more guidance from the community.. 

Otherwise, if you wish, your husband can also submit a complaint to PIBA’s complaint department: tz@piba.gov.il.

Lastly, I'm not sure if it's relevant to your case, but it should be noted that PIBA usually doesn't process partner-visa applications while the Israeli partner is out of the country. Short trips abroad are unlikely to cause meaningful delays, but extended trips certainly can - it is something we at AIC have seen in a number of cases. Just worth noting.
